prd.name: alder
prd.provenance: Consolidates the original RFC (notes1), the extension/dependency addendum (notes2), and two review rounds that corrected the composition algebra, error model, data-role hierarchy, and numerical-backend boundary.

vision.thesis: An Alder program is an immutable value that may be fitted only on data marked for fitting, and that produces an immutable, audited, typed function from an input X to a prediction P. For preprocessing, fitting also produces the exact transformed training observations that may safely be passed to the next stage — and the type system tracks who may consume them.
vision.centralContribution: Prepared: a fitted artifact plus leakage-safe training rows, governed by a preparation-scope discipline. Target-independent preparation is reusable; cross-fitted target-dependent preparation is terminally consumable; anything beyond that requires explicit whole-chain cross-fitting. No mainstream framework names this distinction.
vision.governingPrinciple: The compiler rejects category errors, laws test semantic obligations, and runtime validation handles data-dependent facts. No layer pretends to do another layer's job.
audience: Application authors composing preprocessing and models into leakage-safe workflows
Third-party model authors: new ML models target Alder's three unfitted traits as THE interface
Coding agents implementing models against a small, explicit, law-checked SPI

designPrinciples.name: Restraint rule
designPrinciples.rule: A type parameter belongs in the public API only when changing it changes which programs are legal.

designPrinciples.name: Lawfulness over convenience
designPrinciples.rule: The safe API only states laws that are actually true. Where the industry-standard shortcut violates a law (e.g. pooled-OOF standardization), Alder refuses to certify it, offers a lawful alternative at similar cost, and reserves the shortcut for the explicitly unstable SPI where no law is claimed.
designPrinciples.framing: The restriction is about lawfulness, not a claim of large practical bias. Second-order leakage through pooled statistics is real but O(1/n) for smooth statistics; docs must not overstate its magnitude.

designPrinciples.name: No universal estimator
designPrinciples.rule: There is no Estimator base class, no isFitted, no clone protocol, no reflective parameter maps, no runtime capability tags, no metadata routing. Unfitted values simply lack prediction operations; capabilities are typeclass evidence; metadata requirements are context bounds (WeightOf[M], GroupOf[M], TimeOf[M]).

designPrinciples.name: Fitted artifacts never travel without their audit
designPrinciples.rule: Trained[A] pairs the artifact with a mandatory Audit. Audit construction is framework-owned via FitContext; plugins supply only identity, version, validated config, and backend fingerprint.

designPrinciples.name: Alder owns statistics, not linear algebra
designPrinciples.rule: Alder owns statistical algorithms and small fused loops (Welford moments, standardization). It owns no general-purpose linear-algebra kernel. Gale is the preferred numerical implementation substrate behind optional adapters — never Alder's public ontology of what a matrix is.

buildAndCompatibility.rationale: TASTy compatibility is one-directional: newer compilers read older minor-version TASTy, not the reverse. Publishing the kernel from 3.7.x would exclude LTS-pinned plugin authors. Gale and linop4s both publish from 3.3.8. No post-3.3 language feature is needed anywhere in the public API.

compatibilityGates.mima: from the first published release (0.1), not deferred
compatibilityGates.evolutionPolicy: New functionality arrives via extension methods, final helper classes, and capability typeclasses — never by adding abstract members to frozen traits.

compilerFlags.note: Source-quality policy for Alder's own build only; never a consumer requirement. -Yexplicit-nulls may be relaxed in Java-interop-heavy backend modules.

kernelDependencies.rationale: One stable Cats dependency beats a bespoke miniature Cats hidden inside an ML framework (EitherT, Eq, monoids, law interop).

buildAndCompatibility.crossBuild: Pure modules (kernel, laws, data, preprocess, metrics, tune, models-linear) cross-build JVM + Scala.js + Scala Native from day one — Native CI is the forcing function that keeps the kernel platform-clean (required for kernel+laws, advisory for the rest). Backend adapters follow their libraries: alder-ridge-linop4s all three platforms, alder-ridge-gale JVM + JS.

rules: Ordinary fitting accepts NonEmptyData[U, A] for U <: Use.Fit.
Tuning accepts only NonEmptyData[Use.Train, A]; no overload accepts evaluation data.
No public asTrain / retag / unsafePromote. Promotion happens through narrow audited constructors only.

refitProtocol.afterFinalEvaluation: Refit.after(finalEvaluationReceipt).from(split.allObserved) — receipt-gated promotion of all labelled observations
refitProtocol.auditObligation: The refit audit records sources (train+validation[+test]), the authorizing evaluation receipt, and the sentence: this refitted artifact has not itself been evaluated on that test set.

types: final class NonEmptyData[+U <: Use, +A] private[alder] (val data: Data[U, A])
final class Holdout[A] private[alder] (val train: NonEmptyData[Use.Train, A], val test: Data[Use.Test, A])
data.rowIdentity: Every logical row carries a stable internal RowId supporting split-disjointness checks, out-of-fold reconstruction in original order, leakage tracing in law tests, and auditable fold lineage.

accessSpi.semanticPath: def foldRows[B](initial: B)(step: (B, RowId, A) => B): B
hotPaths: def foreachBatch(size: BatchSize)(step: RowBatch[A] => Unit): Unit
trait RowBatch[+A] { def length: Int; def rowId(index: Int): RowId; def value(index: Int): A }
accessSpi.rationale: foldRows alone allocates per row; batched access must exist before the SPI is frozen.

observations: final case class Example[+X, +Y, +M](input: X, target: Y, meta: M)
final case class Scored[+Y, +P, +M](truth: Y, prediction: P, meta: M)
data.metadataCapabilities: M is real application data, never Map[String, Any]. Requirements are typeclasses visible in signatures: WeightOf[M], GroupOf[M] { type Key }, TimeOf[M]. A grouped resampler requires GroupOf; rolling-origin requires TimeOf; weighted learners/metrics require WeightOf. There is no metadata router.

schemas.applicationSchemas: Case classes and enums, e.g. final case class House(...) derives Schema, Coordinates, CanEqual

definition: def writeTo(value: A, destination: CoordinateWriter): Either[CoordinateError, Unit]
rules: Derivation succeeds only for complete numeric products; Option[Double] fields do not derive — imputation must first produce a complete type.
None, null, NaN, and 'missing' are never treated as interchangeable.
writeTo is the non-allocating hot path (e.g. straight into a gale DMatBuilder or an operator workspace).

schemas.dynamicVectors: Dense[S] / Sparse[S] carry a runtime schema fingerprint plus a semantic phantom feature-space brand S. Learned dimensions are validated runtime values, never type-level naturals. Sparse[S] is not public in 0.1.

sparsePreprocessingPolicy.problem: Mean-centering densifies sparse data: per-row, (x − μ) makes structural zeros nonzero. sklearn handles this with a runtime error (with_mean=True on sparse input); Alder makes the invalid state unrepresentable instead.
rules: Sparsity-preserving preprocessing exists as Sparse[S] => Sparse[S] transforms (scale-only standardization: x ⊙ invStd keeps zeros zero; the config ADT for the sparse scaler simply has no centering case).

Representation changes are explicit, auditable transforms: Densify[S]: Transform[F, Sparse[S], Dense[S]] (and Sparsify where lawful). A user who wants centered sparse data must say so in the plan, and the cost appears in the plan fingerprint.

Centering that a MODEL needs (e.g. ridge's unpenalized intercept) is not a preprocessing stage at all — it is backend-owned algebra, already specified: gale adapters use means-correction formulas without materializing centered data; linop4s composes the rank-one update X − 1μᵀ as a lazy operator, which is exactly what its inspectable expression tree is for.
Serving is unaffected either way: a Pipe densifying one row at a time is cheap; the hazard is only fit-time materialization of n dense rows.
sparsePreprocessingPolicy.court: Alder owns the type-level policy, the explicit-densification ergonomics, and the laws (scale-only preserves the sparsity pattern; densification never happens implicitly). Backends own centering-by-algebra when a model policy requires it. gale owns efficient sparse value-array operations.

definition: final def andThen[E2, C](next: Pipe[B, E2, C]): Pipe[A, E | E2, C]
final def mapError[E2](f: E => E2): Pipe[A, E2, B]
pipe.decision: Error is a covariant type parameter, not a refinement-type member. Explicit parameters compose with unions naturally and are mechanically easier for plugin authors and coding agents than Pipe[X, Z] { type Error = E } bounds.

definition: final case class Failure[+E] private[alder] (stage: StagePath, cause: E):
failure.rationale: A naked E1 | E2 cannot say which stage failed when stages share an error type. The union is the cause type; Failure carries provenance. StagePath is allocated from the normalized logical plan, not runtime Chain nesting, so parenthesization changes neither stage identities, seed derivations, nor first-failure paths.

errorModel.fitResult: type FitResult[F[_], E, A] = EitherT[F, Failure[E], A]
errorModel.unionSemantics: Scala 3 unions are associative and commutative ((A | (B | C)) =:= ((A | B) | C)), so the cause set is parenthesization-invariant. Fit errors remain associated type members (chosen once per implementation); combinators expose unions (left.FitError | right.FitError). Applications collapse growing unions deliberately via mapFitError/mapRunError — information loss is explicit, never automatic.
errorModel.replayErrors: Because Transform.fit owns its training replay, replay failure surfaces inside that transform's FitError (e.g. case ReplayFailed(error: RunError)). Composed FitError is exactly left.FitError | right.FitError — no hidden third channel.

preparationScopes.note: Reusable extends LearnerReady (corrected from sibling design): target-independent preparation is a fortiori safe for a terminal learner, so covariance grants LearnerReady consumption for free; the extra privilege (feeding another fitted stage) remains Reusable-only.

semantics.Reusable: No target information was used. Rows may feed another Transform, a FeatureMap, or a Learner.
semantics.LearnerReady: Each row was prepared without its own target (cross-fitted). Rows may feed a terminal Learner only; feeding another preprocessing stage requires whole-chain cross-fitting.

definition: final class Prepared[+S <: Preparation, +U <: Use.Fit, +A, +B] private[alder] (
rules: rows is a protocol resource, not a collection: it is not publicly extractable. Sanctioned combinators inside Alder consume it; summaries/receipts/lineage are publicly inspectable.

The Reusable factory takes only the fitted pipe plus the fitting data and PERFORMS THE REPLAY ITSELF — the input-only replay law is true by construction and cannot be violated by a third party. Score-reuse optimizations (e.g. PCA scores materialized during fit) live in alder.unsafe.spi where the law suite polices them.
FeatureMap's LearnerReady rows are deliberately NOT required to equal replaying the final fitted pipe.

transform.role: Target-blind preprocessing. Cannot inspect Y or M because they do not occur in its input.
definition: def fit[U <: Use.Fit](data: NonEmptyData[U, X])(using FitContext)
: FitResult[F, FitError, Prepared[Preparation.Reusable, U, Fitted, Z]]
transform.correction: fit returns Prepared (not merely Trained): Transform ∘ Transform needs the first stage's prepared rows, and the replay that produces them can fail — each stage owns its replay and its replay errors.

definition: trait FeatureMap[F[_], X, Y, M, Z]:
def fit[U <: Use.Fit](data: NonEmptyData[U, Example[X, Y, M]])(using FitContext)
: FitResult[F, FitError, Prepared[Preparation.LearnerReady, U, Fitted, Example[Z, Y, M]]]

safeConstructors.inputOnly: FeatureMap.inputOnly(transform) — lifts a Transform; library preserves targets, metadata, row identities; result scope is Reusable.
safeConstructors.crossFitted: FeatureMap.crossFitted(encoder: FoldEncoder, resampler) — owns the protocol: split; fit each analysis partition; encode only its held-out assessment partition; reassemble OOF rows in original order; fit one final serving state on all rows; record both lineages. There is deliberately no public encoder.fit(all).encode(all) shortcut.

definition: trait FoldEncoder[F[_], X, Y, M, Z]:
def fit(data: NonEmptyData[Use.Train, Example[X, Y, M]])(using FitContext): FitResult[F, FitError, State]
def encode(state: State, input: X): Either[RunError, Z]

composition.law: FoldEncoder[F, X, Y, M, Z] ∘ Transform[F, Z, W] = FoldEncoder[F, X, Y, M, W] (encoder.andThen(transform))
composition.semantics: The inner transform is fitted per-fold on analysis rows only — whole-chain cross-fitting for the two-stage case, true by construction, at the cost of k+1 inner fits instead of 1.
composition.motivation: Restores the flagship pattern (target-encode then standardize then learn) inside the safe API, which the composition table otherwise outlaws: crossFitted(targetEncoder.andThen(standardizer), folds).learnWith(lr). REQUIRED for 0.1.

learner.role: Terminal learning algorithm. May depend on all training targets because its in-sample predictions are not passed downstream.
definition: trait Learner[F[_], X, Y, M, P]:
def fit[U <: Use.Fit](data: NonEmptyData[U, Example[X, Y, M]])(using FitContext)
learner.terminality: Feeding a model's in-sample predictions into a second learner is the wrong protocol; calibration/stacking/distillation go through explicit CrossFit.predictions(baseWorkflow, folds).learnWith(calibrator). Pure prediction postprocessing stays easy: trained.mapPrediction(Decision.argmax).

abstractions.serving: Effectful/remote/native inference is compiled separately: trait Serving[F[_], -X, +P] { type Error; def predict(input: X): F[Either[Error, P]] }. Local Pipe inference is pure.
abstractions.trained: final class Trained[+A] private[alder] (val artifact: A, val audit: Audit). Constructed only via FitContext.complete.

compositionAlgebra.decision: There is no Workflow trait. 'Workflow' is a descriptive word for a composed Learner. Composition closes over the three unfitted abstractions.

lawfulCompositions.note: a pure already-fitted pipe was not fitted on these rows; scope is preserved
inner transform fitted per-fold on analysis rows; the 0.1 route to target-encode-then-standardize

lawfulCompositions.why: second-order leakage: pooled statistics fitted on OOF rows reintroduce own-target dependence through other rows

leakageModel.rowwiseLaw: row r was not used directly to fit the state producing row r — NECESSARY BUT INSUFFICIENT
leakageModel.transitiveLaw: r ∉ transitiveTargetDependencies(outputFor(r)) — the target of row r must be absent from the entire dependency closure of the representation produced for r
leakageModel.counterexample: Encoder folds A={1,2}, B={3,4}. z3, z4 were fitted using y1, y2. A target-blind standardizer fit on pooled OOF rows has μ depending on y1 through z3, z4; therefore (z1 − μ)/σ depends on y1 despite the standardizer never inspecting a target.
leakageModel.magnitudeHonesty: The dependence is O(1/n) for smooth pooled statistics; pooled-OOF standardization is universal practice in sklearn/mlr3/tidymodels. Alder's docs frame the restriction as lawfulness (the rowwise law is simply false there), not as a claim of material bias.
leakageModel.learnerExemption: The terminal learner may depend on all targets; the moment its predictions feed calibration or stacking, the entire preceding chain must again be cross-fitted.

futureWork.wholeChainCrossFitting: CrossFit.whole(first, second, outer) / first.nestedWith(second, outer): for every outer fold, fit the entire preceding pipeline (including inner cross-fitting) on outer analysis rows; fit downstream preprocessing inside that analysis set; apply only to outer assessment rows; reassemble in original order; fit one serving chain on all data. DEFERRED past 0.1 — one target-aware preprocessing boundary per ordinary workflow is the principled initial restriction; FoldEncoder.andThen covers the common case.

compositionAlgebra.combinatorObligations: Combinators (ThenTransform, LearnedWith, ...) know nothing algorithm-specific. They own: preparation scope, row identity, audit composition, child FitContexts (context.forChild(ordinal)), error widening, lineage. Seeds derive from root seed + normalized plan fingerprint + stable stage ordinal; parenthesization must not change stage seeds, audit paths, or fitted behavior.

predictionSemantics.rule: Prediction semantics are the result type, never a string mode. Typical: Double, Distribution[Class], Class, Ranking[Item], SurvivalCurve[Time], Quantiles[Probability, Double], Gaussian.
predictionSemantics.decisions: A probabilistic classifier is Learner[F, X, Class, M, Distribution[Class]]; a hard decision is a separate pure pipe (Decision.argmax). Metrics get honest input types: LogLoss requires Distribution[C]; Accuracy requires C. Mixing them without an explicit decision rule does not compile.
predictionSemantics.semanticValues: Distribution, Probability, Positive, NonNegative, PositiveInt etc. are opaque types with controlled constructors: dynamic values return typed validation results; literal constructors validate at compile time (NonNegative.const(-0.1) does not compile).

rules: Evaluation streams/parallelizes without changing the public metric (partition law).
Default numerical metrics use reproducible mergeable accumulators; a FastMath mode may trade bitwise reproducibility for speed but must appear in the audit and applicable law set.
Weighted metrics are different values with different requirements (weightedRmse[M: WeightOf]), never optional arguments.

space.rule: Space[A] is applicative, not monadic: every emitted value is a complete, valid A. No tune()/unknown() sentinels; no partially valid configs. Conditional structure is an explicit sum type (enum TreeShape). Data-dependent spaces are ordinary functions FeatureSchema => Space[A].

erasure.rule: Path-dependent Model types are kept (they power ArtifactCodec[learner.Model], Explain, PrincipalComponents on stable values). Tuning erases them deliberately at the boundary via eraseModel — named to say capabilities are being discarded — producing LearnerView[F, X, Y, M, FitE, RunE, P] with Trained[Pipe[X, RunE, P]].

study.rule: A study accepts training data only (NonEmptyData[Use.Train, ...]); no overload accepts evaluation data. It returns Selection[C](best config, trials, StudyAudit) — a selected configuration, not an existentially typed fitted artifact. Final refitting uses the concrete family(selection.best) on Use.Refit data, retaining the path-dependent Model.

rules: Part of the result of fitting, not an experiment-tracker side channel.
Raw data need not be embedded; the fingerprinting policy (digest, source identity, privacy-preserving summary) must itself be recorded.

fitContext.definition: final class FitContext private[alder] — a final framework-owned class, NEVER a trait. Third parties consume it, never implement it; final classes gain compatible methods without breaking plugins.
fitContext.completeProtocol: context.complete(artifact, trainedOn, component: ComponentDescriptor) constructs Trained[A]. The framework supplies stage path, data fingerprint, root/derived seeds, numeric mode, parent lineage, schema fingerprint, child audits. The plugin supplies only ComponentDescriptor(id, version, validated parameters as AuditValue, backend fingerprint). Plugins cannot omit framework-level provenance.

solverReceipt.rationale: Alder-owned neutral schema. linop4s Termination/SolveResult/Evidence map into it (Constructed/NumericallyChecked/UserAsserted -> AssumptionEvidence.*); the original library value may ride in an adapter-specific extension. Optional backends never enter the kernel's audit schema.

provenance.determinism: Given equal plan, data fingerprint, seed, backend fingerprint, and deterministic numeric mode, fitting is observationally repeatable. Nondeterministic backends must say so in NumericMode.

capabilities.rule: A model exposes only typed prediction. Everything else is typeclass evidence: ArtifactCodec[A], Explain[A, X], Incremental[L], PrincipalComponents[A], InverseTransform[A]. Missing evidence means the operation does not compile — there is no runtime 'unsupported'.
codecLaws: decode(encode(model)).predict(x) == model.predict(x) for all valid x; audit round-trips without semantic loss.
Chain codec: ArtifactCodec derivation for Pipe.Chain given codecs of the parts — REQUIRED, or no composed workflow can ever be saved.
Java serialization is not an artifact format.

numericalBackends.boundaryRule: A third-party component pays for: the protocol + the numeric representation it actually uses + the solver it explicitly selects. Nothing else.

backendNeutrality.rule: Solver interfaces consume Alder-owned views (typed data + Coordinates, batched rows, CoordinateWriter), never a Gale matrix. Gale's DMat/DVec must not become Alder's interchange types: that would leak Gale's JDK 21 floor into every plugin and force the linop4s backend through a Gale representation.

gale.role: Preferred numerical implementation substrate (dense QR/Cholesky/LU, sparse, spectral, optional Vector-API/FFM-BLAS acceleration), behind adapter artifacts only.
gale.facts: Scala 3.3.8, JVM+JS, gale-core has zero compile-scope third-party dependencies, JDK 21 floor (22+ for FFM modules), own law suites, Breeze differential parity tests.

ridgeStrategies.NormalCholesky: solve (XᵀX + λI) β = Xᵀy — faster; squares the condition number; gale detects A.t * A structurally (syrk path) and addToDiagonal supplies λI

gale.intercept: Unpenalized intercept via centring: centre X and y, solve for coefficients, reconstruct intercept = mean(y) − mean(X)ᵀ β.
gale.backendCapture: The gale Backend given MUST be captured as a constructor field and fingerprinted at construction (GaleRidgeBackend(galeBackend, strategy, numericMode)). Never summon an ambient Backend inside solve — otherwise BackendFingerprint and the determinism law lie. Fingerprint includes gale version, backend report, native provider, thread config, strategy, numeric mode, centring/weighting policies, tolerances.
gale.gaps: Gale has no statistics (no colMeans/variance) and no elementwise vector algebra (no Hadamard, no vector division). Alder owns Welford/pairwise moments and standardization loops over IArray[Double] / CoordinateWriter.
gale.releasePrerequisite: Gale is 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT, unpublished, with inconsistent coordinates (io.github.canardlapin in build vs io.gale in docs). Sequence: settle org → cut gale 1.0.0 → add compat gates → pin Alder → publish alder-ridge-gale. publishLocal/source-dependency during development only; no stable Alder release depends on a snapshot.

linop4s.role: Genuinely independent second backend (matrix-free LinearMap/AdjointOp + Krylov: CG, MINRES, LSQR) and the stress test proving the backend boundary works.
linop4s.facts: Scala 3.3.8, JVM+JS+Native, core depends on cats-core + algebra only, capability types (PositiveDefinite etc.) with evidence, pure step-machine solvers, rich Termination ADT.

ridgeMapping.lsqr: Damped LSQR minimizes ||Ax−b||² + damp²||x||², so damp = sqrt(λ), NOT λ. Intercept handled by centring so it is not damped.
ridgeMapping.cg: PositiveDefinite.normalEquation(operator, λ) is a sound capability route; the audit must disclose normal-equation conditioning consequences.

linop4s.independence: gale and linop4s have no relationship to each other and Alder must not force one. Two separate adapter artifacts double as the proof of backend neutrality.
linop4s.agreementValue: Agreement between Gale QR/Cholesky and linop4s LSQR/CG is far stronger law-suite evidence than agreement between two wrappers over the same solver.

removedModules.alder-workflow: never existed as a trait; composition closes over the three abstractions

pipe: associativity (output, first failure, stage path, seed allocation all parenthesization-invariant)
transform: training replay: prepared rows equal the fitted pipe applied to original fitting inputs (true by construction via the Reusable factory)
featureMap: target and metadata preservation (only input may change)
single production of every prepared row
preparationConsumption: Reusable preparation may feed another fitted preprocessor.
LearnerReady preparation may feed a terminal learner.
LearnerReady preparation cannot feed a Transform or FeatureMap through the safe API.
A pure fitted Pipe applied rowwise preserves preparation scope.
laws.crossFitExclusion: For every out-of-fold prepared row, that RowId is absent from the fitting lineage of the state that produced its output. Tested with instrumented datasets/encoders recording every visible RowId — the actual protocol is tested, not the implementation's declaration.
laws.futureTransitiveLaw: For every prepared output row r: r is absent from the transitive closure of target dependencies of every fitted state contributing to that output. (Activated with whole-chain cross-fitting.)
learner: score coherence: score(model, e) == model(e.input).map(p => Scored(e.target, p, e.meta))
serving coherence: scoring transforms inputs with the same fitted pipe used by serving
deterministic fitting under equal plan/data/seed/backend/numeric mode
metric: partition law: concatenated partitions == merged accumulators finished once
permutation law: reordering does not change exact results; numerical modes state tolerances
space: validity: every emitted value is a complete valid A
seed law: equal space, strategy, seed yield identical ordered candidates
codec: round trip preserves audit and prediction behavior
chain codec round trip for composed models
laws.backendAgreement: Gale AugmentedQR, Gale NormalCholesky, linop4s LSQR, linop4s CG agree on admissible problems within declared numerical policies — over predictions, objective residuals, and KKT evidence, never bitwise coefficients where the solution is nonunique. Ridge-specific: zero penalty + full rank agrees with OLS within declared tolerance; KKT residual within solver tolerance; coefficient count equals Coordinates[X].size; no successful nonfinite prediction.
laws.algorithmSpecific: Implementations add their own (e.g. sparse PCA compares learned subspace/reconstruction, not raw component matrices — sign/permutation-equivalent bases must not be treated as different).

extensibility.principle: New ML models look at Alder for the interface. The extension surface is three traits plus Pipe, errors, and a law suite.

decisionTree.targetAwarePreprocessing: implement FoldEncoder and use FeatureMap.crossFitted (optionally FoldEncoder.andThen for per-fold downstream stages); custom protocols go to the explicitly unstable SPI
decisionTree.dimensionalityReductionNote: Sparse PCA and kin are Transforms (fitted projection, target-blind), not Learners; a supervised variant is a cross-fitted FeatureMap.

deliverables: AGENTS.md at repository root: implementer decision tree, FitContext.complete contract, exact dependency recipes, law-suite acceptance checklist, compile-negative examples
alder-sparse-pca as a real published reference plugin (the notes2 walkthrough made compilable and law-tested)
No registration files, reflection, package scanning, global catalogues, or engine strings — implementations are ordinary Scala values
extensibility.thirdPartyDependencyGraph: plugin-core -> alder-kernel (+ alder-data optionally); plugin-backend -> plugin-core + the solver library the plugin author chose. alder-laws enters test scope only and never the runtime graph.

openDecisions.question: Full PreparationLineage schema details — deliberately deferred until FeatureMap.crossFitted implementation forces them; the three binding commitments are recorded in D15.

decisionLog.decision: Publish from Scala 3.3.8 LTS; advisory CI on Scala Next.
decisionLog.rationale: TASTy reads old-from-new only; gale/linop4s are 3.3.8; no post-3.3 feature needed. Original notes1 target of 3.7.4 rejected.

decisionLog.decision: Pipe error is a covariant type parameter; FitError/RunError stay associated members on unfitted traits; unions compose; Failure[E] carries StagePath.
decisionLog.rationale: Refinement-type bounds are hostile to plugin authors and agents; naked unions lose stage provenance.

decisionLog.decision: No Workflow abstraction; composition closes over Transform/FeatureMap/Learner; a workflow IS a composed Learner.
decisionLog.rationale: Smaller surface; terminality preserved; combinators own protocol concerns.

decisionLog.decision: Adopt the transitive leakage law; FeatureMap∘Transform and FeatureMap∘FeatureMap are excluded from the safe API; Preparation scopes with Reusable <: LearnerReady.
decisionLog.rationale: Pooled statistics on OOF rows reintroduce own-target dependence through other rows; the rowwise law is insufficient. Reusable is strictly stronger, hence a subtype.

decisionLog.decision: Transform.fit returns Prepared and owns its training replay; the safe Reusable factory performs the replay itself.
decisionLog.rationale: Replay can fail (surfaces in FitError); by-construction replay makes the replay law unviolable; score-reuse goes to unsafe SPI.
Restores target-encode→standardize→learn lawfully (per-fold inner fits are whole-chain cross-fitting for the two-stage case); without it the algebra outlaws the flagship example.

decisionLog.decision: Gale is the implementation substrate behind adapter artifacts; backends consume Alder-owned views, never DMat; gale Backend captured and fingerprinted at construction.
decisionLog.rationale: Prevents JDK-floor leakage, keeps linop4s genuinely independent, keeps determinism claims honest.

decisionLog.decision: linop4s is the second ridge backend (damped LSQR with damp=sqrt(λ), CG via PositiveDefinite.normalEquation); its ADTs map into an Alder-owned SolverReceipt.
decisionLog.rationale: Structurally different implementation makes backend-agreement laws meaningful; optional libraries must not enter the kernel audit schema.

decisionLog.decision: Use.Fit supertype with Train and Refit; refit via audited receipt-gated constructors; tuning accepts Train only.
decisionLog.rationale: 'No retagging ever' was too absolute; deployment refitting is standard and must be explicit, audited, and honest about unevaluated refits.

decisionLog.decision: Tuning erases via eraseModel to LearnerView; Selection returns the winning config; final refit retains the concrete path-dependent Model.
decisionLog.rationale: Uniform types where iteration needs them; capability-bearing concrete types everywhere else.

decisionLog.decision: FitContext is a final framework-owned class with a public constrained complete(...) factory.
decisionLog.rationale: Third parties consume, never implement; final classes evolve compatibly; framework provenance cannot be omitted (corrects notes1's Trained.internal).

decisionLog.decision: Data SPI includes foldRows plus foreachRow/foreachBatch and Coordinates.writeTo before freezing.
decisionLog.rationale: Per-row boxed folds cannot be the only path through the hot loop of every fit.

decisionLog.decision: All Alder artifacts (and the sparse-PCA reference plugin) publish under io.github.canardlapin; gale's docs are corrected to match its build (io.github.canardlapin), no vanity domain.
decisionLog.rationale: io.github groups verify on Sonatype in minutes; cross-org Maven dependencies are normal; a future org.typelevel migration would be a coordinate break at a major boundary regardless. Resolves O1.

decisionLog.decision: Single RidgeBackend taking a RowWeights ADT (Uniform | ByRow — a first-class case, never an absent optional); paired learner values with WeightedRidgeRegression requiring WeightOf[M].
decisionLog.rationale: Learner-side pre-scaling would rebuild scaled X through Coordinates.build (allocation plus 'scaled House' semantics); backends apply sqrt-weights where it is free (gale during DMatBuilder materialization, linop4s as a diagonal operator). Type-level evidence stays at the learner, mirroring the metric design. Weighted cases enter the backend-agreement laws, catching weighted-centring divergence. Resolves O2.

decisionLog.decision: PreparationLineage: three binding commitments now — (1) plan-shaped and per-fold in production audits (fold membership as resampler fingerprint + seed + assignment digest; per-row RowId lists only in the instrumented testkit), (2) every fingerprint carries its policy tag (ContentDigest(algo) | SourceIdentity(uri, version) | Summary(policyId)), (3) Audit/lineage types are final classes with accessors, not case classes. Full schema deferred to crossFitted implementation (O6).
decisionLog.rationale: Per-row lineage in production is a size and privacy hazard; final classes on the frozen surface can gain fields compatibly where case classes cannot. Resolves O3.

decisionLog.decision: Pure modules cross-build JVM + JS + Native from day one (Native required in CI for kernel+laws, advisory elsewhere); backend adapters follow their libraries.
decisionLog.rationale: Dependencies are cats-only and linop4s proves the 3.3.8 Native toolchain; removing a platform is a break while continuous Native CI is the forcing function that keeps the kernel platform-clean; yields a working Native ridge path via the linop4s backend. Resolves O4.

decisionLog.decision: FoldEncoder.andThen admits chains, with a coherence law: encoder.andThen(t1).andThen(t2) is observationally equal to encoder.andThen(t1.andThen(t2)), including stage paths and seeds.
decisionLog.rationale: Transform composition is already closed, so forbidding chains would be an unenforceable syntactic distinction; implementation is identical (fit the composed transform per fold). Linear k+1 cost per appended stage is documented and recorded in lineage. Prepending needs no FoldEncoder support: Transform ∘ FeatureMap is already lawful. Resolves O5.

decisionLog.decision: Sparse preprocessing: no centering constructor exists for Sparse[S] => Sparse[S] transforms (scale-only preserves sparsity); representation changes are explicit audited Densify/Sparsify transforms; model-required centering (ridge intercept) is backend-owned algebra (gale means-correction, linop4s rank-one operator X − 1μᵀ), never a preprocessing stage.
decisionLog.rationale: Turns sklearn's runtime error (with_mean on sparse) into a compile-time absence; fit-time densification becomes impossible silently and visible when chosen; the backend boundary already owned intercept centring, so the sparse case falls out of the existing design. See dataProtocol.schemas.sparsePreprocessingPolicy.
